recent_posts.title: Avalonia 12 released with major performance gains and mobile improvements
recent_posts.summary: Avalonia 12.0 has been released, marking a major foundational update to the cross-platform .NET UI framework. Key highlights include up to 1,867% FPS improvement in complex scenes, 3x Android performance gains (startup time dropping from 1,960ms to 460ms with NativeAOT), and the first native Linux accessibility backend (AT-SPI2) in any .NET framework. The release ships a built-in page-based navigation system (ContentPage, DrawerPage, CarouselPage, TabbedPage), themeable client-side window decorations, an overhauled focus management system, and improved dispatcher APIs closer to WPF conventions. The WebView component has been open-sourced. Wayland support groundwork is laid and in private preview. The codebase has been cleaned up by targeting .NET 10 and SkiaSharp 3.0, removing netstandard2.0, Direct2D1, Tizen, and Blazor support. Hundreds of bug fixes are included. The team has grown to 19 people backed by a $3M Devolutions sponsorship.

recent_posts.title: Retiring Accelerate: One Brand, One Clear Path
recent_posts.summary: Avalonia UI is retiring the 'Accelerate' brand with the release of Avalonia 12, consolidating everything under a single product with five clear tiers: Free, Community (now non-commercial only), Plus, Pro, and Enterprise. Existing Accelerate subscribers keep their pricing permanently and gain Charts as a bonus. The Community tier's eligibility is tightening from a revenue-threshold model to strictly non-commercial use, after widespread abuse of the honor system. A JetBrains-style individual vs. organizational licensing split is being introduced. Organizations currently using Community commercially will receive a 50% transition discount.

recent_posts.title: Avalonia UI adds mobile support for iOS and Android in early preview
recent_posts.summary: Avalonia UI is expanding beyond desktop to support mobile platforms (iOS and Android), as well as the browser. Early adopters can get started with a sample Wordle port that runs on Desktop, Browser, iOS, and Android, plus dotnet templates (`avalonia.xplat`) and documentation. Mobile support is in early/preview phase ahead of the planned 11.0 release in early Summer. Desktop remains production-ready.

recent_posts.title: Announcing the release of TreeDataGrid
recent_posts.summary: Avalonia UI has publicly released TreeDataGrid, a new open-source control combining DataGrid and TreeView functionality. It is designed for high performance with large datasets, featuring virtualization and strongly typed bindings. The control is available for free under the MIT license via NuGet, though issue and pull request support is limited to paying customers. It currently lacks data editing capabilities but is already used in production by commercial customers.

recent_posts.title: Thoughts on Avalonia
recent_posts.summary: Nick Polyak, a software architect and CodeProject author, shares his journey from WPF to Avalonia. He describes Avalonia as a multiplatform WPF++ that matches and exceeds WPF's concepts while adding cross-platform support for Windows, Linux, Mac, and browsers via WebAssembly. He highlights Avalonia's advantages over UWP, Xamarin, and web frameworks, noting its flexible visual tree, Reactive Extensions-based bindings, and ease of adoption for WPF developers. Nick also mentions his open-source contributions including UniDock (a docking framework), theming/localization tools, and a series of beginner tutorials on CodeProject.

recent_posts.title: Case Study - Fluent Search
recent_posts.summary: Adir Hudayfi, a Microsoft engineer, shares his experience building Fluent Search — a Spotlight-like productivity app for Windows — using Avalonia UI. He explains why he chose Avalonia over WPF and UWP, highlighting its superior performance, modern Fluent design support (including Windows 11 Mica effect), and flexibility. He argues Avalonia is currently the best option for .NET desktop app developers, even for Windows-only projects, and praises its active open-source community and fast bug resolution.

recent_posts.title: Case Study - Lunacy
recent_posts.summary: Icons8's Lunacy team shares their experience porting a Windows-only WPF graphic design application to Avalonia UI, achieving cross-platform support across Windows, macOS, iOS, and more. They highlight Avalonia's similarity to WPF as a key advantage that reduced porting time by an estimated 3x, praise its CSS-like styling system, open-source code quality, and active community. Minor gaps like IME and right-to-left text support were noted but are being addressed.

recent_posts.title: MAUI Avalonia Preview 1
recent_posts.summary: The first preview of Avalonia.Controls.Maui has been released, enabling .NET MAUI apps to run on Linux and WebAssembly using Avalonia's drawn UI backend. Setup requires just four steps: create a MAUI app, add the NuGet package, target net11.0, and call UseAvaloniaApp on the MauiBuilder. The backend provides cross-platform UI consistency as an alternative to native controls, and was validated by porting real apps including AlohaAI and MyConference. SkiaSharp.Views.Maui and GraphicsView-based libraries are supported with minimal or no changes. Future plans include a bespoke Maui.Essentials implementation and WinUI interoperability.

recent_posts.title: Avalonia 12.0 Preview 1
recent_posts.summary: Avalonia 12.0 Preview 1 is now available, marking the first in a series of staged previews ahead of a stable release. The release focuses on performance and stability rather than new features. Key highlights include Android performance improvements (new dispatcher, GPU/CPU fixes, multiple activity support), iOS scene delegate and Mac Catalyst support, a new TextOptions API with LetterSpacing as an inherited property, a new GroupBox control, a Focus Traversal API, compiled bindings enabled by default, and INCR clipboard protocol support on Linux X11. Breaking changes include dropping netstandard2.0 and net4x support in favor of .NET 8 as the minimum target, upgrading to SkiaSharp 3.0, and removing Tizen, Direct2D1, Avalonia.Browser.Blazor, and BinaryFormatter support. Documentation is incomplete and Avalonia Accelerate component compatibility is still in progress. The preview is available on NuGet.

recent_posts.title: Accelerate Showcase: Built with AI, Designed with Stitch
recent_posts.summary: A product manager at Avalonia UI built a polished desktop showcase app without writing any code manually, using Claude Code, Google Stitch for UI design, and Avalonia's DevTools and Parcel MCP servers. The workflow involved generating component skills from documentation, prompting Claude to design and implement an MVVM app targeting .NET 10 for Windows/macOS/Linux, and using the Parcel MCP server to handle cross-platform packaging including macOS code signing and notarization. The result was a shippable app produced in roughly an hour, compared to an estimated week of designer-plus-engineer effort. The post highlights where AI is genuinely useful for Avalonia: building applications with it rather than building the framework itself.
